name: Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Complex
dressCode: Modest attire; strictly no electronic devices inside
note: The revered sanctum and prison cell (Garbha Griha) where Bhagwan Krishna took birth. Features the majestic Bhagvat Bhavan and ancient stone carvings.
audio: Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi is the sacred epicenter of Mathura where Bhagwan Krishna incarnated at midnight to Devaki and Vasudeva.

name: Shri Dwarkadhish Temple
note: Famous for intricate Rajasthani architecture, carved pillars, and ecstatic swing festival (Hindola) during monsoon.
audio: Built in 1814 by Seth Gokuldass, Dwarkadhish Mandir showcases Lord Krishna as the majestic King of Dwarka with vibrant frescoes.

name: Vishram Ghat & Yamuna Maha Aarti
timing: Open all day; Evening Maha Aarti at 7:00 PM
dressCode: Footwear removed on the marble ghat steps
note: The central ghat where Krishna rested after defeating tyrant Kansa. Beautiful sunset wooden boat rides and glowing brass aartis.
audio: Vishram Ghat is the jewel of Mathura's 25 holy ghats. Here Lord Krishna rested, and the sacred Yamuna aarti fills the river with shimmering diyas.

name: Bhuteshwar Mahadev Temple
note: One of the four ancient Shiva guardian protectors (Kotwal) of Mathura, protecting the city from negative energies since antiquity.
audio: Bhuteshwar Mahadev is considered the eternal protector of Mathura. Pilgrims offer water and bilva leaves before proceeding on pilgrimage.

name: Gita Mandir (Birla Mandir)
note: Grand red sandstone temple built by the Birla family where all 18 chapters and 700 verses of the Bhagavad Gita are carved on marble pillars.
audio: Gita Mandir features a magnificent life-sized chariot of Lord Krishna and Arjuna, surrounded by peaceful landscaped gardens on Mathura-Vrindavan road.

name: Potara Kund
note: Large octagonal stepped reservoir where Mother Devaki used to wash baby Krishna's baby clothes (potra). Quiet, peaceful heritage site.
audio: Potara Kund is an ancient stepped water tank associated with Krishna's infancy, featuring massive red sandstone steps.

name: Kans Qila (Kansa Fort Ruins)
note: Ancient riverfront fort ruins on Yamuna banks, restored by Raja Man Singh of Amber with an observatory built by Sawai Jai Singh.
audio: Kans Qila stands as a testament to Mathura's antiquity, offering commanding views of the Yamuna and old city ghats.

name: Chamunda Devi Temple
note: Revered Shaktipeeth temple near Mathura where a lock of Mother Sati's hair is believed to have fallen. Highly auspicious during Navratri.
audio: Shri Chamunda Devi Temple is one of Mathura's powerful Shakti sanctums, visited by pilgrims seeking divine protection and courage.

name: Mathura Government Museum
note: World-renowned museum housing the finest collection of red sandstone Kushana and Gupta era sculptures, headless statue of King Kanishka, and Buddhist relics.
audio: Founded in 1874 by F.S. Growse, the Mathura Museum holds globally celebrated masterworks of ancient Indian terracotta and stone sculpture.

name: Shri Keshav Dev Ji Temple
note: The original historic seat of Lord Keshavdev consecrated by Vajranabh, Great-grandson of Krishna, located adjacent to the Janmabhoomi sanctum.
audio: Keshavdev Temple was historically rebuilt multiple times by rulers including Chandragupta Vikramaditya and Bir Singh Deo Orchha.

name: Holi Gate Bazaar & Brijwasi Sweets
note: Historic bazaar renowned for caramelized Mathura Peda, piping hot Hing Kachori with spicy aloo, and creamy saffron Kulhad Rabri.
audio: Mathura's culinary heritage is legendary. Caramelized khoya pedas prepared over smoldering fire offer an unforgettable taste of Braj.

name: Gokarneshwar Mahadev Temple
note: Ancient northern guardian Shiva lingam situated near Saraswati Kund, associated with sage Gokarna and ancient Vedic yajnas.
audio: Gokarneshwar Mahadev completes the divine protective quadrangle of Lord Shiva safeguarding the holy city of Mathura.

name: Shri Banke Bihari Temple
dressCode: Keep spectacles and bags safe from monkeys
note: Vrindavan's most celebrated deity in Tribhanga posture, manifested by Swami Haridas in Nidhivan. Curtains open and close repeatedly so the Lord's enchanting glance does not overwhelm devotees.
audio: Shri Banke Bihari was manifested by Swami Haridas's divine singing. The Lord is treated with tender love like a playful child.

name: Prem Mandir (Temple of Divine Love)
timing: 5:30 AM - 12:00 PM, 4:30 PM - 8:30 PM (Light show at 7:30 PM)
note: Spectacular Italian Carrara white marble temple complex depicting divine pastimes, featuring a world-famous illuminated musical fountain show.
audio: Conceived by Jagadguru Kripalu Maharaj, Prem Mandir represents pure divine love and radiates vibrant multicolored hues at twilight.

name: ISKCON Krishna Balaram Mandir
dressCode: Modest attire; shoes deposited at entrance
note: Vibrant temple with continuous 24-hour Harinam Sankirtan since 1975, white marble courtyard, and Srila Prabhupada's Samadhi Mandir.
audio: The ISKCON Krishna Balaram Temple in Raman Reti is a global center for bhakti yoga and ecstatic Hare Krishna singing.

name: Nidhivan Sacred Grove
timing: 6:00 AM - 11:30 AM, 4:00 PM - 6:30 PM (Gates close at sunset)
dressCode: Strictly vacate before nightfall; guard eyeglasses from monkeys
note: Mystical grove of intertwined Tulsi trees where Radha and Krishna are believed to perform nocturnal Raas Leela. Houses Rang Mahal and Lalita Kund.
audio: Nidhivan's sacred trees grow in twisted pairs. According to belief, no living being remains inside after the evening Shayan Aarti.

name: Shri Radha Raman Temple
note: Houses the exquisitely self-manifested deity of Krishna carved from a sacred Shaligram Shila by Gopal Bhatta Goswami. The sacred kitchen fire has burned without interruption for over 500 years.
audio: Shri Radha Raman manifested on Vaishakha Purnima in 1542. His radiant smile and delicate features are spiritually captivating.

name: Shri Radha Vallabh Temple
note: Headquarters of the Radha Vallabh sampradaya established by Hith Harivansh Mahaprabhu. Worship emphasizes the supreme devotion to Shri Radha Rani.
audio: In Radha Vallabh Temple, beside the deity of Krishna, a sacred crown is placed to represent the omnipresent divine form of Radha Rani.

name: Shri Radha Damodar Temple
note: Established by Srila Jiva Goswami in 1542. Houses the sacred Govardhan Shila given by Krishna to Sanatana Goswami with Lord Krishna's footprint, calf hoof print, and flute mark.
audio: Four parikramas of the Radha Damodar temple are considered equivalent to completing the full 21 km Govardhan Hill circumambulation.

name: Shri Radha Madan Mohan Temple
note: Vrindavan's oldest standing red sandstone temple standing majestically atop a 50-foot hillock near Kalidaha, built in 1580 by Ram Das Kapur.
audio: Radha Madan Mohan is closely linked with Srila Sanatana Goswami and serves as a classic landmark of medieval Braj architecture.

name: Keshi Ghat & Sunset Yamuna Aarti
timing: Open all day; Sunset Aarti at 6:30 PM
dressCode: Footwear removed on the bathing steps
note: Vrindavan's most magnificent Yamuna riverfront ghat where Lord Krishna bathed after defeating the fierce demon Keshi who took horse form.
audio: Sunset at Keshi Ghat features glowing floating lamps on the holy Yamuna and stunning tiered sandstone Rajasthani architecture.

name: Govind Dev Ji Temple
note: A 1590 architectural marvel built by Raja Man Singh of Amer using red sandstone. Originally 7 stories tall, combining Hindu and medieval palace design.
audio: Govind Dev Ji Temple was once visible for miles with its monumental vaulted dome, celebrating Lord Krishna's appearance as Govinda.

name: Gopeshwar Mahadev Temple
note: The unique temple where Lord Shiva is worshipped as a Gopi. In the evening, the Shiva lingam is dressed in feminine saree, shringar, and jewelry.
audio: To enter the sacred Maha Raas dance, Lord Shiva took Gopi form after bathing in Mansarovar. Krishna affectionately named him Gopeshwar.

name: Sewa Kunj & Nikunj Van
note: Walled sacred garden containing a central Krishna-Radha shrine where Krishna lovingly decorated and braided Radha Rani's hair before Raas.
audio: Sewa Kunj is revered as the sanctum of divine loving service, filled with twisted trees, peaceful parikrama paths, and Lalita Kund.

name: Shri Priya Kant Ju Temple
note: Stunning modern lotus-flower shaped temple standing 125 feet high on the Mathura-Vrindavan highway, founded by spiritual teacher Devkinandan Thakurji.
audio: Surrounded by water ponds with evening colorful illumination, Priya Kant Ju temple is a breathtaking sight on the Chhatikara approach.

name: Shahji Temple (Chhedi Walon Ka Mandir)
note: Built in 1876 by wealthy merchant Shah Kundan Lal of Lucknow. Famous for 12 spiral twisted marble pillars and the Basanti Kamra with rare Belgian chandeliers.
audio: Shahji Temple's Basanti Kamra opens only twice a year and features yellow silk wall hangings and ornate Austrian crystal lamps.

name: Shri Radha Shyamasundar Temple
note: One of the historic seven Goswami temples. The deity was manifested from the sacred heart of Shyamananda Pandit after he found Radha's divine anklet.
audio: Radha Shyamasundar Temple has an exceptionally sweet devotional mood, venerating Srimati Radharani's pure transcendental love.

name: Kaliya Dah & Sacred Kadamba Tree
note: The ancient Yamuna ghat containing the 5000-year-old surviving Kadamba tree from which boy Krishna leapt into the poisoned whirlpool to tame Kaliya Naag.
audio: Here Krishna performed the Kaliya Mardan dance on the serpent's hundred hoods, purifying the Yamuna waters for all Braj devotees.

name: Imli Tala (Sacred Tamarind Tree)
note: Ancient tamarind tree on Yamuna bank where Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu sat in 1515, absorbed in intense Krishna Prema, chanting the holy names.
audio: Imli Tala dates back to Satya Yuga. Krishna sat under this tree immersed in longing for Radha during the Raas Leela.

name: Maa Vaishno Devi Ashram
note: Features the world's tallest 141-foot statue of Goddess Vaishno Devi riding a lion, with realistic cave water walkways and a free spiritual museum.
audio: Maa Vaishno Devi Ashram provides pilgrims an inspiring cave pilgrimage simulation alongside a charitable hospital and goshala.

name: Raman Reti Sacred Sands
dressCode: Remove footwear to walk in sacred sand; modest clothing
note: The holy soft white sands where child Krishna and Balaram rolled, tumbled, and played with cowherd boys. Features an idyllic deer sanctuary and hermitage.
audio: Pilgrims from around the world joyfully roll in the blessed sands of Raman Reti to receive the divine touch of baby Krishna's lotus feet.

name: Chaurasi Khamba (84 Pillars Palace)
note: Ancient palace of Nanda Maharaj in Old Gokul (Mahavan) built with 84 intricately carved stone pillars, representing the 84 lakh life species.
audio: Chaurasi Khamba marks the palace where Yashoda cradled infant Krishna. It is one of the oldest preserved stone sanctums in the Mathura district.

name: Brahmand Ghat
timing: Open all day; Evening Aarti at 6:30 PM
dressCode: Footwear removed on the riverside steps
note: The sacred Yamuna ghat where toddler Krishna ate clay dirt. When Mother Yashoda scolded him, he opened his mouth and revealed the entire cosmic universe.
audio: At Brahmand Ghat, the Brahmand Bihari temple overlooks the gentle Yamuna river where pilgrims collect consecrated holy earth (Mridika).

name: Nand Bhavan (Gokul Palace)
note: The childhood home where baby Krishna lived after being carried across the flooded Yamuna by Vasudeva to save him from Kansa.
audio: Nand Bhavan celebrates Krishna's sweet early childhood. Priests sing traditional Braj folk lullabies welcoming devotees to rock the Lord's cradle.

name: Ukhal Bandhan Ashram
note: Where Mother Yashoda tied naughty Krishna to a heavy wooden mortar (Ukhal). Krishna dragged the mortar and liberated two demigods trapped as Yamalarjuna trees.
audio: Ukhal Bandhan reveals Krishna as Damodara, the Supreme Lord who willingly allows himself to be bound only by the pure rope of love.

name: Chintaharan Mahadev Temple
note: Quiet Yamuna-side Shiva temple where Yashoda prayed to Lord Shiva to take away all evil eyes and anxieties (chinta) regarding her darling child Krishna.
audio: Offering milk and jal at Chintaharan Mahadev is believed to dispel worldly stress, worries, and planetary afflictions.

name: Pootna Moksha Sthal
note: The pasture field where infant Krishna sucked out the life air of the demoness Pootna, granting her the eternal exalted status of a mother in the spiritual world.
audio: This pastime illustrates the supreme causeless mercy of Krishna, who accepted even a poisoner as a foster mother because she offered her breast milk.

name: Yashoda Ghat & Baithakji
note: Peaceful Yamuna ghat where Mother Yashoda washed clothes and bathed baby Krishna. Contains a revered Vallabhacharya Baithakji.
audio: Yashoda Ghat offers serene sunset views of the Yamuna with traditional wooden boats and sweet breezes of rural Gokul.

name: Shri Radha Rani Temple (Ladli Ji Mandir)
dressCode: Stair climbing or ropeway pass; modest clothing
note: Perched majestically on Bhanugarh hill overlooking scenic Barsana. Birthplace of Shri Radha Rani and world-famous epicenter of Lathmar Holi.
audio: Shri Radha Rani temple, also known as Shriji Mandir, is a 250-step palatial shrine radiating unmatched joy and devotion in Braj.

name: Rangeeli Mahal & Kirti Mandir
note: Breathtakingly carved pink stone temple complex dedicated to Mother Kirti and baby Radha, featuring lush gardens and divine illuminated statues.
audio: Kirti Mandir is the only temple in the world celebrating Shri Radha's mother, Kirti Maiya, holding infant Radharani in her lap.

name: Maan Mandir (Maan Garh Peak)
note: Peak where Radha took divine loving offense (maan) and Krishna pacified her by dressing as a peacock. Base of Ramesh Baba's massive cow sanctuary housing 50,000+ cows.
audio: Maan Mandir commands panoramic views of the Aravalli ridges of Braj and stands as a beacon of Yamuna revival and cow protection.

name: Dan Bihari Temple
note: Historic temple commemorating where Krishna stopped the Gopis and demanded a loving tax (dan) of butter, milk, and sweet devotion.
audio: Dan Bihari temple in the narrow gorge of Sankari Khor reflects the joyful tax-collection pastimes of youth Krishna in Barsana.

name: Priya Kund (Pili Pokhar)
note: Sacred pond where Mother Yashoda applied turmeric to Radha's hands before an auspicious ceremony, turning the entire pond golden (pili).
audio: Priya Kund is surrounded by Kadamba trees where pilgrims sit quietly reflecting on the pre-marital sweet bonds between Nandgaon and Barsana.

name: Mor Kuti (Peacock Dance Sanctum)
note: Hilltop pavilion where Radha and Krishna assumed peacock forms and danced together to the music of gathering monsoon rainclouds.
audio: At Mor Kuti, hundreds of wild peacocks still gather every morning and evening, dancing gracefully around the hill shrine.

name: Sanket Van
note: The mystical grove situated exactly halfway between Nandgaon and Barsana, where Radha and Krishna had their first romantic meeting by pre-arranged signal (sanket).
audio: Sanket Van contains a scenic Kund and a quiet temple celebrating the eternal meeting of the divine couple.

name: Prem Sarovar
note: Sacred pond manifested from the divine tears of love shed by Radha and Krishna during an ecstatic trance of loving separation.
audio: Surrounded by leafy groves and stone steps, Prem Sarovar is considered the liquid embodiment of transcendental divine love.

name: Nandgaon (Nand Bhawan Temple)
note: Hilltop palace fortress on Nandishwar Hill where Krishna lived with Nanda Baba and Yashoda from ages 6 to 10. Famous for festive Samaj Gayan.
audio: Nandgaon is the village of Nanda Maharaja. The main temple houses charming deities of Krishna, Balarama, Nanda, Yashoda, and cowherd friends.

name: Pavan Sarovar
note: Sacred lake at the base of Nandishwar hill where Yashoda bathed Krishna after grazing cows. Sanatana Goswami resided here in a small bhajan kutir.
audio: Pavan Sarovar is revered as one of the four principal lakes of Braj, celebrated for the evening coolness of its waters.

name: Govardhan Hill (Giriraj 21 km Parikrama)
timing: Parikrama path open 24 hours (Best walked early morning or night)
dressCode: Soft cotton socks or walking shoes
note: 21 km sacred circumambulation of the holy hill lifted by 7-year-old Krishna on his left pinky finger for 7 days to shield Braj from Indra's torrential storm.
audio: Govardhan Hill is non-different from Lord Krishna Himself. Completing the 21 km circuit brings deep spiritual fulfillment and peace.

name: Shri Daan Ghati Mandir
dressCode: Modest attire; milk pot offering counters outside
note: The epicenter of Govardhan town where the deity of Giriraj Ji is naturally embedded in the roadside rock, anointed continuously with streams of fresh milk.
audio: Daan Ghati marks where Krishna collected milk toll from the Gopis before permitting them to pass through the narrow hill path.

name: Kusum Sarovar
dressCode: Remove footwear on the stone terrace steps
note: Majestic 460-foot reservoir framed by ornate tiered red sandstone chhatris (cenotaphs) built in 1764 by Maharaja Jawahar Singh of Bharatpur in honor of Maharaja Suraj Mal.
audio: Kusum Sarovar is adorned with painted ceiling frescoes depicting the pastimes of Krishna and the royal court of Bharatpur.

name: Radha Kund & Shyam Kund
timing: Open all day; Holy bathing during Bahulashtami at midnight
dressCode: Traditional bathing attire; footwear strictly removed
note: The supreme sanctum of Gaudiya Vaishnavism. Twin sacred lakes created by Krishna (Shyam Kund) and Radha (Radha Kund) after slaying the Arishta bull demon.
audio: Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu rediscovered Radha Kund in 1515. It is revered as the highest spiritual place in the entire material and spiritual universe.

name: Mukharbind Mandir (Jatipura)
note: The sacred mouth (Mukharbind) of Giriraj Maharaj in Jatipura, celebrated by Vallabhacharya devotees who offer Panchamrit, milk bhog, and grand 56-bhog Annakut.
audio: At Mukharbind, devotees witness the miraculous stone face of Giriraj being lovingly anointed with hundreds of liters of fresh cow milk.

name: Haridev Mandir
note: Ancient temple overlooking Manasi Ganga consecrated by Krishna's great-grandson Vajranabh, where Krishna holds Govardhan with his left hand.
audio: Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu ran ecstatically to embrace Haridev upon reaching Govardhan, weeping tears of pure divine joy.

name: Manasi Ganga Kund
note: The central lake of Govardhan manifested directly from Krishna's mind (manas) so his elderly parents would not have to travel all the way to Haridwar to bathe in Ganga.
audio: Bathing in Manasi Ganga before beginning the Govardhan Parikrama grants a pilgrim the full benefit of bathing in Mother Ganga.

name: Poochari Ka Lautha
note: Marks the tail end of Govardhan hill where Krishna's friend Lautha Baba sits awaiting Krishna's return from Mathura. Devotees offer milk and dhoop.
audio: Poochari Ka Lautha reflects the deep, unwavering friendship between Krishna and his dear cowherd companions.
